_review: // REVIEW: Educational seed content. Human clinical verification required before public launch. Not exhaustive; no diagnosis or prescribing guidance.

conditions.name: Migraine
conditions.summary: Migraine is a neurological condition causing recurring attacks of headache and other symptoms. Treatment can relieve attacks or help prevent them.

sex_differences.summary: Migraine occurs more often in women than in men. Hormonal changes can trigger attacks.

conditions.name: Tension-type headache
conditions.summary: This common headache causes pressure or tightness around the head. Stress and muscle tension can contribute.

conditions.name: Open-angle glaucoma
conditions.summary: Damage to the optic nerve can gradually reduce vision. Lowering pressure inside the eye helps slow progression.

conditions.name: Allergic rhinitis
conditions.summary: The immune system reacts to airborne allergens in the nose. Symptoms may be seasonal or year-round.

conditions.name: Acute otitis media
conditions.summary: Inflammation and infection affect the middle ear. Antibiotics are used for selected bacterial cases; some cases improve with observation.

conditions.name: Temporomandibular disorder
conditions.summary: Problems in the jaw joint or chewing muscles can cause pain and restricted movement. Conservative care is often the starting point.

conditions.name: Dental caries
conditions.summary: Acids made by bacteria damage the hard surface of a tooth. Pain medicines may ease symptoms but do not repair the decay.

conditions.name: Streptococcal pharyngitis
conditions.summary: Group A streptococcal bacteria cause an infection of the throat. Testing helps distinguish it from viral causes.

conditions.name: Hypothyroidism
conditions.summary: The thyroid does not make enough thyroid hormone. Replacement treatment supports normal metabolism.

conditions.name: Neck strain
conditions.summary: Muscles or tendons in the neck are overstretched. Recovery usually involves gradual movement and rehabilitation.

conditions.name: Asthma
conditions.summary: Inflamed, sensitive airways narrow at times and make breathing difficult. Reliever medicines and long-term anti-inflammatory treatment have different roles.

conditions.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
conditions.summary: Persistent airway obstruction makes it harder to move air out of the lungs. Treatment can improve symptoms and reduce exacerbations.

conditions.name: Chronic stable angina
conditions.summary: Reduced blood flow to the heart can cause predictable chest discomfort with exertion. New, severe, or changing chest pain needs urgent medical assessment.

conditions.name: Gastroesophageal reflux (GERD)
conditions.summary: Stomach contents repeatedly flow into the esophagus and cause troublesome symptoms. Acid-reducing medicines can help symptoms and healing.
nonDrugTreatments: Avoid lying down soon after meals

conditions.name: Rib fracture
conditions.summary: A rib breaks after trauma or repeated stress. Pain relief supports breathing while the bone heals.

conditions.name: Irritable bowel syndrome with constipation
conditions.summary: IBS involves recurring abdominal pain and changes in bowel habits. This subtype is mainly associated with constipation.

conditions.name: Occasional constipation
conditions.summary: Stools can become hard or difficult to pass. Fluid, dietary, and activity changes may help alongside short-term symptom treatment.

conditions.name: Ulcerative colitis
conditions.summary: Immune-driven inflammation affects the lining of the colon. Treatment aims to control inflammation and maintain remission.

conditions.name: Uncomplicated bacterial cystitis
conditions.summary: Bacteria cause an infection in the bladder. Antibiotic selection depends on the clinical situation; nitrofurantoin is not used for kidney infections.

conditions.name: Overactive bladder
conditions.summary: The bladder signals a sudden need to urinate, sometimes with leakage. Behavioral approaches and medicines may help.

conditions.name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
conditions.summary: A noncancerous enlarged prostate can restrict urine flow. Treatment depends on symptom severity and complications.

conditions.name: Primary dysmenorrhea
conditions.summary: Menstrual cramps occur without an underlying pelvic disease. Prostaglandins contribute to uterine cramping.

conditions.name: Lower back strain
conditions.summary: Muscles or tendons in the lower back are overstretched or torn. Gradual return to movement is commonly part of recovery.

conditions.name: Rotator cuff tear
conditions.summary: One or more shoulder tendons are partly or fully torn. Medicines can ease pain but do not repair the tear.

conditions.name: Lateral elbow tendinopathy
conditions.summary: Repeated loading can damage tendons on the outer elbow. Rehabilitation and load management are central to recovery.

conditions.name: Forearm fracture
conditions.summary: One or both forearm bones break after injury. Pain relief is supportive while alignment and stability are addressed.

conditions.name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
conditions.summary: Compression of the median nerve at the wrist affects sensation and sometimes hand strength. Medicines are not the primary treatment.

conditions.name: Hand osteoarthritis
conditions.summary: Joint tissues gradually change and cartilage is lost in affected hand joints. Treatment focuses on pain, function, and daily activities.

conditions.name: Wrist sprain
conditions.summary: Ligaments around the wrist are overstretched or torn. Assessment helps distinguish a sprain from a fracture.

conditions.name: Knee osteoarthritis
conditions.summary: Changes in cartilage and other joint tissues can cause knee pain and stiffness. Exercise and strength work are important parts of management.

conditions.name: ACL tear
conditions.summary: The anterior cruciate ligament helps stabilize the knee. A tear can cause instability; pain medicines support comfort but cannot restore the ligament.

conditions.name: Hamstring strain
conditions.summary: Muscle fibers at the back of the thigh are overstretched or torn. Progressive rehabilitation helps restore strength and movement.

conditions.name: Shin splints
conditions.summary: Repeated loading causes pain along the shinbone. Training changes and gradual rehabilitation are central to treatment.

conditions.name: Ankle sprain
conditions.summary: Ankle ligaments stretch or tear when the joint twists. Rehabilitation helps restore balance and stability.

conditions.name: Plantar fasciitis
conditions.summary: The tissue supporting the foot arch becomes painful, commonly near the heel. Loading changes and stretching are main treatments.

conditions.name: Athlete’s foot
conditions.summary: A superficial fungal infection affects the skin of the feet. Keeping the area dry supports topical treatment.

conditions.name: Atopic dermatitis
conditions.summary: A disrupted skin barrier and immune inflammation cause recurring itchy patches. Treatment supports the skin barrier and controls flares.

conditions.name: Acne vulgaris
conditions.summary: Blocked follicles and inflammation cause pimples and other lesions. Treatment depends on the type and severity of acne.

conditions.name: Minor superficial burn
conditions.summary: Heat damages the outer layer of skin. Larger, deeper, chemical, electrical, or sensitive-area burns need prompt medical assessment.

conditions.name: Urticaria
conditions.summary: Histamine release causes raised, itchy welts. Breathing difficulty or throat swelling requires emergency care.
nonDrugTreatments: Identify and avoid triggers where possible

conditions.name: Type 1 diabetes
conditions.summary: The immune system destroys insulin-producing cells. Insulin replacement is essential and commonly includes basal and mealtime components.

conditions.name: Type 2 diabetes
conditions.summary: The body becomes less responsive to insulin and may not make enough of it. Management is individualized to overall health and glucose levels.

conditions.name: Hypertension
conditions.summary: Blood pressure stays elevated over time. Management reduces the risk of damage to the heart, kidneys, brain, and blood vessels.

conditions.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
conditions.summary: An autoimmune disease can inflame several organs and tissues. Treatment varies substantially with organ involvement and disease activity.

conditions.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
conditions.summary: The immune system attacks joint tissue and can affect other organs. Disease-modifying medicines help control inflammation and limit joint damage.

conditions.name: Hyperlipidemia
conditions.summary: Elevated blood lipids can contribute to plaque in arteries. Treatment is guided by cardiovascular risk as well as lipid levels.

conditions.name: Epilepsy
conditions.summary: Epilepsy causes recurrent unprovoked seizures from abnormal electrical activity in the brain. Antiseizure treatment is tailored to seizure type.

conditions.name: Concussion
conditions.summary: A concussion is a brain injury caused by a blow or sudden movement of the head. Recovery requires a gradual return to normal activity after assessment.
nonDrugTreatments: Brief relative rest followed by a guided return to activity

conditions.name: Dry eye
conditions.summary: Dry eye occurs when tears do not adequately lubricate the eye. Treatment depends on tear production, eyelid health and environmental triggers.

conditions.name: Cataract
conditions.summary: A cataract clouds the eye's natural lens. Surgery can replace the cloudy lens when vision loss affects daily life.

conditions.name: Otitis externa
conditions.summary: Otitis externa is inflammation or infection of the outer ear canal, often after water exposure. Appropriate ear drops are selected after examining the ear.
nonDrugTreatments: Keep the ear dry during treatment

conditions.name: Tinnitus
conditions.summary: Tinnitus is the perception of sound without an external source. Management addresses contributing hearing problems and the impact on sleep or concentration.

conditions.name: Acute bacterial sinusitis
conditions.summary: Bacterial sinusitis can follow a respiratory infection and cause persistent or worsening sinus symptoms. Antibiotics are reserved for cases meeting clinical criteria.

conditions.name: Nosebleed
conditions.summary: Bleeding can occur when small vessels inside the nose are injured or irritated. Persistent or heavy bleeding needs medical assessment.
nonDrugTreatments: Firm pressure to the soft nose while leaning forward

conditions.name: Gingivitis
conditions.summary: Gingivitis is inflammation of the gums, commonly caused by dental plaque. Professional cleaning and effective oral hygiene are the main treatments.

conditions.name: Oral thrush
conditions.summary: Oral thrush is an overgrowth of Candida yeast in the mouth. Antifungal treatment and addressing predisposing factors help clear infection.
nonDrugTreatments: Review inhaler technique or other contributing factors

conditions.name: Jaw fracture
conditions.summary: A jaw fracture is a break in the jawbone following trauma. Pain relief supports care but cannot restore bone alignment.

conditions.name: Jaw dislocation
conditions.summary: A dislocated jaw occurs when the jaw joint moves out of position. A trained clinician may need to return it to its normal position.

conditions.name: Rosacea
conditions.summary: Rosacea causes recurring facial redness and sometimes acne-like bumps. Treatments control symptoms and are chosen for the pattern of disease.

conditions.name: Impetigo
conditions.summary: Impetigo is a contagious superficial bacterial skin infection. Limited infections may be treated with a topical antibiotic, while more extensive disease needs clinical review.

conditions.name: Viral pharyngitis
conditions.summary: Viral pharyngitis is a sore throat caused by a viral infection. Supportive care relieves symptoms; antibiotics do not treat the virus.
nonDrugTreatments: Clinical assessment if severe or persistent

conditions.name: Acute laryngitis
conditions.summary: Laryngitis is inflammation of the voice box, often during a viral infection or after voice overuse. Persistent hoarseness needs evaluation.

conditions.name: Vocal fold nodules
conditions.summary: Vocal fold nodules are benign growths associated with repeated voice strain. Voice therapy is usually central to management.

conditions.name: Hyperthyroidism
conditions.summary: Hyperthyroidism means the thyroid produces excessive thyroid hormone. Antithyroid medicines are one option for hormone overproduction, depending on its cause.
nonDrugTreatments: Radioactive iodine or surgery in selected cases

conditions.name: Subacute thyroiditis
conditions.summary: Subacute thyroiditis is painful inflammation of the thyroid that can temporarily alter hormone levels. Anti-inflammatory treatment can relieve pain while thyroid function is monitored.

conditions.name: Cervical spondylosis
conditions.summary: Cervical spondylosis describes age-related changes in the neck's discs and joints. Treatment is guided by symptoms and any nerve or spinal cord involvement.
nonDrugTreatments: Surgical assessment for significant nerve compression

conditions.name: Atrial fibrillation
conditions.summary: Atrial fibrillation is an irregular heart rhythm that can increase stroke risk. Apixaban is an example of stroke prevention for eligible patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation; it does not correct the rhythm.

conditions.name: Heart failure
conditions.summary: Heart failure occurs when the heart cannot pump or fill effectively enough for the body's needs. Lisinopril is one component of care for selected patients with reduced pumping function.

conditions.name: Community-acquired pneumonia
conditions.summary: Pneumonia is infection of lung tissue. Amoxicillin is one option for selected uncomplicated bacterial cases; treatment depends on severity and the likely organism.

conditions.name: Lactational mastitis
conditions.summary: Mastitis is breast inflammation during lactation that may become bacterial. Antibiotics are used when bacterial mastitis is suspected, alongside supportive lactation care.

conditions.name: Breast cyst
conditions.summary: A breast cyst is a fluid-filled sac within breast tissue. Many need no treatment, but new lumps require assessment and painful cysts may be drained.

conditions.name: Hormone receptor-positive breast cancer
conditions.summary: This breast cancer subtype can respond to treatments that block estrogen signaling. Tamoxifen is an option for selected patients within a specialist treatment plan.

conditions.name: Costochondritis
conditions.summary: Costochondritis is pain and inflammation where ribs join the breastbone. Chest pain requires assessment to distinguish it from cardiac or other serious causes.
commonSymptoms: Pain with movement or deep breathing

conditions.name: Achalasia
conditions.summary: Achalasia prevents normal relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter and disrupts swallowing. Procedures that reduce resistance at the sphincter are common treatments.

conditions.name: Hiatal hernia
conditions.summary: A hiatal hernia occurs when part of the stomach moves through the diaphragm into the chest. Acid suppression treats associated reflux symptoms, not the hernia itself.

conditions.name: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia
conditions.summary: This birth defect leaves an opening in the diaphragm, allowing abdominal organs to enter the chest. It requires specialist stabilization and surgical care.

conditions.name: Peptic ulcer disease
conditions.summary: Peptic ulcers are sores in the stomach or duodenal lining. Acid suppression helps healing; Helicobacter pylori infection requires a complete eradication regimen when present.
nonDrugTreatments: Test and treat the underlying cause

conditions.name: Gastritis
conditions.summary: Gastritis is inflammation of the stomach lining with several possible causes. Treatment addresses the cause, and acid suppression may help selected patients.

conditions.name: Chronic hepatitis B
conditions.summary: Chronic hepatitis B is persistent infection of the liver with hepatitis B virus. Selected patients benefit from antiviral treatment to suppress the virus and reduce liver damage.

conditions.name: Chronic hepatitis C
conditions.summary: Chronic hepatitis C is persistent hepatitis C virus infection that can damage the liver. Direct-acting antiviral combinations can cure many infections after appropriate assessment.

conditions.name: Cirrhosis
conditions.summary: Cirrhosis is advanced liver scarring caused by chronic injury. Treatment depends on the cause and complications rather than one medicine for every patient.

conditions.name: Gallstones
conditions.summary: Gallstones are hardened deposits in the gallbladder. Symptomatic stones may require removal of the gallbladder or treatment of an obstructed bile duct.
nonDrugTreatments: Endoscopic treatment of duct stones when indicated

conditions.name: Acute pancreatitis
conditions.summary: Acute pancreatitis is sudden inflammation of the pancreas. Treatment often requires hospital care to support hydration, nutrition and pain control while treating the cause.
nonDrugTreatments: Intravenous fluids and nutrition support as indicated

conditions.name: Chronic pancreatitis
conditions.summary: Chronic pancreatitis causes lasting pancreatic damage and may reduce digestive enzyme production. Pancreatic enzyme replacement helps patients with resulting maldigestion.
nonDrugTreatments: Endoscopic or surgical care when indicated

conditions.name: Kidney stones
conditions.summary: Kidney stones are hard deposits that can obstruct urine flow and cause severe pain. Pain relief is supportive; stone size, obstruction and infection determine further treatment.
nonDrugTreatments: Stone removal or lithotripsy when needed

conditions.name: Chronic kidney disease
conditions.summary: Chronic kidney disease is persistent loss of kidney function or evidence of kidney damage. An ACE inhibitor may help selected patients with hypertension or albuminuria, with monitoring of kidney function and potassium.
nonDrugTreatments: Dialysis or transplantation for kidney failure

conditions.name: Splenic injury
conditions.summary: Trauma can tear the spleen and cause internal bleeding. Management depends on stability and injury severity, and requires urgent medical assessment.

conditions.name: Splenomegaly
conditions.summary: Splenomegaly means an enlarged spleen and can result from infection, liver disease or blood disorders. Treatment targets the underlying cause.
nonDrugTreatments: Avoid activities that risk abdominal trauma

conditions.name: Acute appendicitis
conditions.summary: Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix that can progress to rupture. Urgent assessment determines surgical care or a selected antibiotic-based approach.

conditions.name: Appendiceal neuroendocrine tumor
conditions.summary: A neuroendocrine tumor can arise in the appendix and is sometimes found after appendectomy. Treatment depends on tumor size, location and spread.

conditions.name: Hemorrhoids
conditions.summary: Hemorrhoids are swollen vascular cushions in the anus or lower rectum. Treatment focuses on easier bowel movements and procedures for persistent symptoms.
nonDrugTreatments: Office procedures or surgery when indicated

conditions.name: Anal fissure
conditions.summary: An anal fissure is a small tear in the anal lining, often after passage of hard stool. Reducing constipation helps healing, with specialist treatment for persistent fissures.
commonSymptoms: Small amounts of bright red blood

conditions.name: Thoracic vertebral compression fracture
conditions.summary: A compression fracture collapses part of a vertebral body. Pain relief supports treatment while the cause, stability and nerve function are assessed.

conditions.name: Osteoporosis
conditions.summary: Osteoporosis weakens bone and increases fracture risk. Alendronate is one option for patients who meet treatment criteria.
nonDrugTreatments: Adequate calcium and vitamin D intake

conditions.name: Lumbar disc herniation
conditions.summary: A herniated lumbar disc can irritate nearby nerve roots. Many cases improve with conservative care; progressive neurological symptoms need urgent assessment.

conditions.name: Spinal cord injury
conditions.summary: Trauma to the spinal cord can disrupt movement, sensation and autonomic function. Emergency stabilization and rehabilitation are central to care.

conditions.name: Multiple sclerosis
conditions.summary: Multiple sclerosis damages myelin in the central nervous system. Baclofen can relieve spasticity; separate disease-modifying treatment is chosen by a specialist.
nonDrugTreatments: Neurology care and disease-modifying treatment planning

conditions.name: Coccydynia
conditions.summary: Coccydynia is pain around the tailbone, often after pressure or trauma. Care focuses on relieving pressure and improving function.

conditions.name: Sacral fracture
conditions.summary: A sacral fracture is a break in the bone at the base of the spine. Management depends on stability, bone health and nerve involvement.

conditions.name: Shoulder bursitis
conditions.summary: Shoulder bursitis is inflammation of a fluid-filled cushion around the joint. Treatment reduces irritation and restores comfortable movement.

conditions.name: Adhesive capsulitis
conditions.summary: Adhesive capsulitis, or frozen shoulder, causes progressive pain and restricted shoulder motion. Recovery often requires sustained rehabilitation.

conditions.name: Humeral fracture
conditions.summary: A humeral fracture is a break in the upper-arm bone. Stabilization and sometimes surgery are needed for healing.

conditions.name: Biceps strain
conditions.summary: A biceps strain stretches or tears muscle or tendon fibers in the upper arm. Rehabilitation restores strength after the initial injury is assessed.

conditions.name: Olecranon bursitis
conditions.summary: Olecranon bursitis affects the fluid-filled cushion over the elbow tip. Infection must be distinguished from pressure-related inflammation.
nonDrugTreatments: Drainage or infection treatment when indicated

conditions.name: Forearm muscle strain
conditions.summary: A forearm strain damages muscle or tendon fibers through overuse or sudden loading. Supportive treatment is followed by gradual restoration of function.

conditions.name: Dupuytren contracture
conditions.summary: Dupuytren contracture thickens tissue beneath the palm and can pull fingers into a bent position. Treatment depends on how much hand function is affected.
nonDrugTreatments: Needle or surgical release when indicated

conditions.name: Hand contusion
conditions.summary: A hand contusion is bruising of soft tissue after a blow. Persistent pain or loss of function warrants assessment for fracture or other injury.

conditions.name: Trigger finger
conditions.summary: Trigger finger occurs when a flexor tendon catches as it moves through its sheath. Splinting, injection or release may be considered depending on severity.

conditions.name: Hip osteoarthritis
conditions.summary: Hip osteoarthritis causes progressive cartilage and joint changes. Medicines may relieve pain, while exercise and joint replacement can improve function in selected patients.

conditions.name: Hip fracture
conditions.summary: A hip fracture is a break near the upper end of the thigh bone. It usually needs urgent orthopedic care and frequently surgery.

conditions.name: Quadriceps strain
conditions.summary: A quadriceps strain damages fibers in the muscles at the front of the thigh. Recovery depends on severity and a gradual return to loading.

conditions.name: Patellofemoral pain syndrome
conditions.summary: Patellofemoral pain causes pain around or behind the kneecap during loading. Exercise-based rehabilitation is the main treatment.

conditions.name: Tibial stress fracture
conditions.summary: A tibial stress fracture is a small bone injury caused by repeated loading. Rest from impact activity allows healing and reduces risk of a larger fracture.

conditions.name: Calf strain
conditions.summary: A calf strain injures muscle fibers at the back of the lower leg. Marked swelling or unexplained pain needs assessment for other causes.

conditions.name: Achilles tendinopathy
conditions.summary: Achilles tendinopathy causes load-related pain in the tendon joining calf muscles to the heel. Pain medicines are supportive; progressive tendon loading is central to treatment.

conditions.name: Ankle fracture
conditions.summary: An ankle fracture breaks one or more bones around the ankle joint. Alignment and stability guide treatment.

conditions.name: Heel contusion
conditions.summary: A heel contusion bruises the soft tissue cushion under the heel. Persistent focal pain requires assessment to exclude a bone injury.

conditions.name: Metatarsal stress fracture
conditions.summary: A metatarsal stress fracture is a small break caused by repeated loading of a forefoot bone. Healing requires reducing the load on the injured bone.

conditions.name: Ingrown toenail
conditions.summary: An ingrown toenail occurs when a nail edge irritates or grows into nearby skin. Persistent or infected cases may need a nail procedure.

conditions.name: Gout
conditions.summary: Gout is inflammatory arthritis caused by urate crystals in joints. Colchicine treats or helps prevent flares; long-term urate control is a separate treatment decision.

conditions.name: Psoriasis
conditions.summary: Psoriasis is an immune-mediated condition that produces inflamed scaly skin. Low-potency topical corticosteroids can help selected mild or sensitive-site disease under appropriate guidance.
nonDrugTreatments: Phototherapy or specialist treatment when needed

conditions.name: Deep vein thrombosis
conditions.summary: A blood clot forms in a deep vein, often in the leg. A piece can break off and travel to the lungs.
nonDrugTreatments: Compression and activity guidance individualized by a clinician

conditions.name: Pulmonary embolism
conditions.summary: A clot blocks a pulmonary artery, often after traveling from a deep vein in the leg. Large blockages can strain the right side of the heart.
nonDrugTreatments: Catheter or surgical clot removal in selected severe cases
